data.title: Code Virtualization / VM-Based Obfuscation
data.summary: A portion of the sample's logic is compiled to a custom bytecode and executed by an embedded interpreter rather than running as native instructions — removing that logic from the disassembler's view entirely.
data.description:
This is the deepest and most expensive form of obfuscation commodity packers offer: rather
than hide the native code, it replaces it with bytecode for a virtual machine unique to
that protector, so a disassembler sees only the interpreter's dispatch loop, never the
protected logic's real instructions. It is typically reserved for licence checks, a single
critical routine, or anti-tamper logic rather than the whole binary, because of the
performance cost.
data.recommendation:
* Identify which specific routine is virtualised rather than attempting to reverse the VM wholesale; it is usually a small, deliberately chosen target.
* Use dynamic tracing (instruction-level or API-level) through the interpreter rather than static disassembly, which will not recover the protected logic.
* Check published devirtualisers for the specific commercial protector in use before building one from scratch.
data.short_recommendation: Trace the protected routine dynamically through the interpreter rather than disassembling it statically.

mitre_techniques.procedure: A licence-check routine executed entirely inside a custom bytecode interpreter embedded in the binary.

mbc_techniques.implementation: One routine was compiled to custom bytecode and run through an embedded dispatch-loop interpreter.
